assessments.reasoning: The SPDX repository’s GitHub tag object 76c9a79bb7d2bf851143b76b3935a4d7cbaa644b names v3.29.0 and targets object type commit, SHA 31ba1a50e5397e00a304dbadc76531740e89ee48, exactly the detail URL revision. GitHub reports the tag unsigned.

The pinned json/details/OGL-UK-1.0.json gives licenseId OGL-UK-1.0, name Open Government Licence v1.0, and isDeprecatedLicenseId false. Both crossRef and seeAlso identify http://www.nationalarchives.gov.uk/doc/open-government-licence/version/1/. The detail’s licenseText also declares version 1.0.
Contextual support for the publisher side comes from the English version declaration at [8586,8636) on the official version/1/ route. SPDX owns the identifier assignment.

challenge.method: Compared tag-object and target SHAs, detail filename and fields, both publisher-link fields, and the inspected publisher declaration. Tested the other UK editions, Canada, a changed retrieval route and literal text equality.
challenge.results: The SPDX HTTP directory reference and inspected HTTPS version/1/open-government-licence.htm differ in scheme and filename. Their host, edition directory and declared edition agree. The alternative originals declare other editions or another government. SPDX records match as the string “false”. Its “Her Majesty’s” differs from the publisher’s “His Majesty’s,” defeating literal equality while preserving the documented link.

limitations: The correspondence is specific to SPDX Data 3.29.0. It establishes neither literal text equivalence nor XML build lineage, approval, or a grant for any particular work. The tag and detail belong to one SPDX information chain.
reasoning: SCES §7 requires an external index assertion to be attributed to its owner and pinned to an exact release or record. The annotated SPDX Data tag targets the commit serving the OGL-UK-1.0 detail. That record explicitly pairs the identifier with the v1.0 name and National Archives version/1/ reference. The government page confirms which edition the reference identifies.
